subject: ACCTG
title: Data Analytics for Accounting
description: Covers data analytics as it pertains to accounting professionals. Data has proliferated in business and managers and accountants need to understand the implications for decision-making and tap into the data to provide better insights into a firm/client/customer/supplier, etc. This course is intended to provide students with an understanding of data analytic thinking and terminology as well as hands-on experience with data analytics tools and techniques. Three major areas that comprise analytics are data reporting, data visualization, and predictive analytics. subject: ASL
title: ASL IV
description: Advanced conversational skills, grammatical structures, classifiers, and narrative are covered in ASL Level IV classes. Offering thorough ASL communication while developing vocabulary and fluency, typically encompassing role-shifting, elaborate descriptions, and culturally relevant Deaf concerns, prepares students for more advanced interactions with native/Deaf signers. Taught in American Sign Language (ASL). No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division ASL course taken in ASL. An ASL Level 4 course builds upon previous ASL knowledge by focusing on advanced conversational skills, complex grammatical structures, an in-depth understanding of ASL classifiers, and nuanced storytelling. Allowing students to engage in detailed ASL communication while further refining their vocabulary and fluency, often including topics like role-shifting, detailed descriptions, and culturally significant issues within the Deaf community; essentially preparing them for more advanced interactions with native/Deaf signers; requiring completion of ASL Level 1, 2, and 3 courses with a grade of ¿C¿ or better, or equivalent as a prerequisite.
prerequisite_text: ASL 201 or equivalent with a grade of ¿C¿ or better. Junior or Senior standing
enrollment_requirements: ASL 201 or equivalent with a grade of ¿C¿ or better. Junior or Senior standing

description: This course will outline the legal environment affecting HR management. subject: B A
title: Hum Resource Mgmt Law II
description: This introduction to California labor and employment law will cover a wide variety of workplace topics including wage and hour law, employee classification, minimum wage and overtime laws, meal and rest period requirements, and other Labor Code requirements. Additional topics include vacation, PTO and sick leave; personnel records and privacy; drug testing and background checks; and confidentiality and company trade secret protection. In addition to understanding how California employment law interacts with the work environment, you'll learn how reduce the risk of employment-related claims and lawsuits. Guest speakers &; specialists in California labor and employment law &; will provide a broad perspective on how specific legal topics affect HR professionals, managers, and employees.

subject: CHEM
title: Intro Gen Chem w/ Lab
description: Survey of the fundamental chemical principles of matter, presenting students with the elementary chemical concepts used to illustrate nature and the development of modern scientific thought. This course is offered as a GE course to students in non-STEM majors and fulfills the General Education Natural Sciences and Quantitative Reasoning requirement. The course is also offered as a General Chemistry course to students in STEM majors that do not require taking Chemistry 200 (e.g. Food and Nutrition major). This course is also recommended as a preparatory course for students with limited mathematics and/or science background who plan to take higher level chemistry courses such as Chemistry 100, or students who plan to take the Chemistry Placement Exam for placement in Chemistry 200. Not open to students with credit in Chemistry 100 or 200.

subject: ENGR
title: Prac App Construction Law
description: Applications of Construction Law online course provides a framework for understanding the legal environment in which construction takes place. Students will learn the stages of contracts, how to avoid litigation, protective methods for the employee/employer in a litigious society, understand the legal liability of construction professionals, avoid disputes using clauses, and be more informed when navigating the legality of the jobsite. Students will learn about the different models of contracts, contract principles, offers, and defenses to the formation of contracts. We will review the Uniform Commercial Code (UCC) and how it is used in sales contracts. Topics also include the roles and responsibilities of the contractor, architect, and the documents that bind them. Bonds, liens, and waivers, the legal liability of construction professionals, avoiding disputes through use of clauses, and how to avoid defects are included in this course.

subject: POL S
title: Inter Diplomacy
description: The search to find new and more effective ways of resolving internal conflicts is a major preoccupation in today's world. The massive toll that modern wars have taken on civilian populations has given great urgency to this search. The violence done to the population through terror, the destruction of personal property, physical injury, and the loss of loved ones all point to the urgent need to build peace in our world. New and innovative approaches to humanitarian intervention and conflict resolution must be developed. New roles and tasks have emerged for international organizations such as the United Nations and the OSCE. At the same time, civil society organizations have increasingly played an important role in conflict resolution through Track II diplomacy, conflict-sensitive approaches to development, and third-party nonviolent intervention.

subject: PSY
title: Statistical Meth in Psych
description: Quantitative methods in psychology for producing, analyzing, and interpreting data. Sampling, basic research designs, describing distributions, correlation, regression, applications of normal probability curve, confidence intervals, and tests of significance. Analysis and interpretation of data using statistical, spreadsheet, and word processing software. Students with credit or concurrent registration in the following lower division statistics courses will be awarded a total of four units for the two (or more) courses: Psychology 280; Administration, Rehabilitation and Postsecondary Education 201; Biology 215; Civil Engineering 160; Economics 201; Political Science 201; Sociology 201; Statistics 119 and 250.

description: International students are advised to take Linguistics 100B. Writing and reading as critical inquiry, designed to help students undertake university-level writing projects. Focus on rhetoric of written arguments. Students learn to use sources in their writing and make appropriate decisions about structure, cohesion, and rhetorical conventions. Not open to students with credit in a higher-numbered composition course or AFRAS 120 or AMIND 120 or CCS 111B or ECL 100 or LING 100B or RWS 105B.

Continued attention to structure, cohesion, and rhetorical conventions. Not open to students with credit in AFRAS 200, AMIND 225, CCS 200, ECL 200, or LING 200. subject: RWS
title: Writing in Various Settings
description: Composing effective texts for a wide range of situations in and out of the university. Learning to adjust textual elements for specific purposes, audiences, and settings. Enhances critical reading and writing skills by exploring how content contributes to meaning and effectiveness. Satisfies the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement (GWAR) for students who get a minimum grade of C or Cr. Upper-division courses should only be taken by students who have completed 60 semester units or more. In exceptional cases, a student who has completed fewer than 60 units may enroll in upper division courses. International students are advised to take LING 305W.

description: Composing effective texts for a wide range of situations in and out of the university. Learning to adjust textual elements for specific purposes, audiences, and settings. Enhances critical reading and writing skills by exploring how content contributes to meaning and effectiveness. Satisfies the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement (GWAR) for students who get a minimum grade of C or Cr. Upper-division courses should only be taken by students who have completed 60 semester units or more. In exceptional cases, a student who has completed fewer than 60 units may enroll in upper division courses. International students are advised to take LING 305W.
prerequisite_text: Completion of lower division GE Area 1. Junior or senior standing. RWS 200, or AFRAS 200, or AMIND 225, or CCS 200, or ECL 200, or LING 200, or PHIL 200, or RWS 220 with a grade of C- (1.7) or better.
enrollment_requirements: Completion of lower division GE Area 1. Junior or senior standing. RWS 200, or AFRAS 200, or AMIND 225, or CCS 200, or ECL 200, or LING 200, or PHIL 200, or RWS 220 with a grade of C- (1.7) or better.

subject: POL S

description: The search to find new and more effective ways of resolving internal conflicts is a major preoccupation in today's world. The massive toll that modern wars have taken on civilian populations has given great urgency to this search. The violence done to the population through terror, the destruction of personal property, physical injury, and the loss of loved ones all point to the urgent need to build peace in our world. New and innovative approaches to humanitarian intervention and conflict resolution must be developed. New roles and tasks have emerged for international organizations such as the United Nations and the OSCE. At the same time, civil society organizations have increasingly played an important role in conflict resolution through Track II diplomacy, conflict-sensitive approaches to development, and third-party nonviolent intervention.

enrollment_requirements: Junior or senior standing.

enrollment_requirements: Junior or senior standing.

enrollment_requirements: AMIND 110. Junior or Senior standing.

enrollment_requirements: ANTH 101.

enrollment_requirements: ANTH 101.

subject: ANTH
title: Principles of Archaelogy
description: History, method, and theory of archaeological data acquisition and interpretation. Methods of data recovery and analysis suitable to resolution of historical and processual questions. Archaeological examples from a worldwide sample of prehistoric and historic societies.
prerequisite_text: ANTH 103.
enrollment_requirements: ANTH 103.

enrollment_requirements: ANTH 103.

subject: ANTH
title: Princ Socio Cultural Anth
description: Development of theories which explain nature of culture and cultural variation. Applications of theory of culture to field methods in ethnography and interpretation of ethnographic findings.
prerequisite_text: ANTH 102.
enrollment_requirements: ANTH 102.

title: Princ Socio Cultural Anth
description: Development of theories which explain nature of culture and cultural variation. Applications of theory of culture to field methods in ethnography and interpretation of ethnographic findings.

enrollment_requirements: ANTH 102.

subject: ANTH
title: Prin of Anth Linguistics
description: Structural nature of language. How languages differ, change and influence each other. Language families of the world. Significance of language for human social life in a variety of cultures.
prerequisite_text: ANTH 102.
enrollment_requirements: ANTH 102.

subject: ANTH
title: Roots of Civilizations
description: The development of human societies around the world from the first stone tools to flourishing cities. Debate what defines a "civilization" and characterize the resilience of ancient societies. How can archaeology teach us lessons for a sustainable future?
prerequisite_text: Junior or Senior standing
enrollment_requirements: Junior or Senior standing

subject: ANTH
title: Exploring Cultural Diversity
description: Diverse cultures from around the world are explored through core anthropological concepts and approaches. In depth cases studies address topics such as religion, gender, personhood, medicine, life/death, artistic expression, environmental adaptation, historical change, and globalization. This course satisfies the general education cultural diversity requirement.
prerequisite_text: Junior or Senior standing.
enrollment_requirements: Junior or Senior standing.

subject: ANTH
title: Sustainability and Cultur
description: Examination of efforts of anthropology to understand sustainability and provide solutions to human-environmental problems. Compares and explores sustainability in a variety of contexts and scales, from San Diego region to diverse communities around the world.
prerequisite_text: Junior or senior standing.
enrollment_requirements: Junior or senior standing.

subject: ANTH
title: Modern Forensic Anth
description: Physical anthropology and skeletal biology within medicolegal context. Methodologies used in science of forensic anthropology, as interdisciplinary nature and authorities in related fields.
prerequisite_text: Completion of the GE requirement in Foundations of Learning II.A. 2. Life Sciences. If a biological sciences course is not taken to satisfy Foundations of Learning II.A. 2., a college course in biological sciences is required. Junior or Senior standing.
enrollment_requirements: Completion of the GE requirement in Foundations of Learning II.A. 2. Life Sciences. If a biological sciences course is not taken to satisfy Foundations of Learning II.A. 2., a college course in biological sciences is required. Junior or Senior standing.

subject: ANTH
title: Archaeolgy of Domestic Animals
description: Examines the long-term relationship humans have with animals. Follows the beginnings of hunting through domestication and examines the rise of modern society's industrial relationship to domesticated animals. This course satisfies the general education cultural diversity requirement.
prerequisite_text: Upper division standing.
enrollment_requirements: Upper division standing.

subject: ANTH
title: Dynamics Biocultural Diversity
description: Explore the interplay of biology and culture in human populations over time and around the world. Using 'systems thinking', examine the impact that various geographies, technologies, political-economic (structural) arrangements, historical legacies, and cultural contexts have on human evolution.
prerequisite_text: Completion of Area 5B. Biological Science General Education requirement. If a biological sciences course is not taken to satisfy Area 5B., a college course in biological sciences is required.
enrollment_requirements: Completion of Area 5B. Biological Science General Education requirement. If a biological sciences course is not taken to satisfy Area 5B., a college course in biological sciences is required.

subject: ANTH
title: Music and Culture
description: How the forms, functions and meanings of music vary crossculturally. Understanding a society's music historically, holistically and experientially, with emphasis on non-Western music. Universals of music and music use. Anthropological theories of music and music change. This course satisfies the general education cultural diversity requirement.
prerequisite_text: Junior or Senior standing.
enrollment_requirements: Junior or Senior standing.

subject: ANTH
title: The Supernatural
description: Magic and religion. Conceptions of the supernatural in a cross section of world's cultures. Anthropological theories relating to supernatural beliefs and practices. Courses for Area (C) Theories and Methods, are identified in the course title as (C). This course satisfies the general education cultural diversity requirement. Same course as REL S 424.
prerequisite_text: Junior or senior standing.
enrollment_requirements: Junior or senior standing.

subject: ANTH
title: The Supernatural

prerequisite_text: Junior or senior standing.
enrollment_requirements: Junior or senior standing.

subject: ANTH
title: Culture on Film
description: Experience anthropology through visual representations of culture. Viewing films, documentaries, photography and animation, we reflect on how these mediums shape our comprehension of diverse human experience through depictions of class, kinship and belonging, conflict and difference, land/sea/cosmos, living and dying. This course satisfies the general education cultural diversity requirement.

subject: ASL
title: ASL IV
description: Advanced conversational skills, grammatical structures, classifiers, and narrative are covered in ASL Level IV classes. Offering thorough ASL communication while developing vocabulary and fluency, typically encompassing role-shifting, elaborate descriptions, and culturally relevant Deaf concerns, prepares students for more advanced interactions with native/Deaf signers. Taught in American Sign Language (ASL). No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division ASL course taken in ASL. An ASL Level 4 course builds upon previous ASL knowledge by focusing on advanced conversational skills, complex grammatical structures, an in-depth understanding of ASL classifiers, and nuanced storytelling. Allowing students to engage in detailed ASL communication while further refining their vocabulary and fluency, often including topics like role-shifting, detailed descriptions, and culturally significant issues within the Deaf community; essentially preparing them for more advanced interactions with native/Deaf signers; requiring completion of ASL Level 1, 2, and 3 courses with a grade of ¿C¿ or better, or equivalent as a prerequisite.

subject: CHEM
title: Intro Gen Chem w/ Lab
description: Survey of the fundamental chemical principles of matter, presenting students with the elementary chemical concepts used to illustrate nature and the development of modern scientific thought. This course is offered as a GE course to students in non-STEM majors and fulfills the General Education Natural Sciences and Quantitative Reasoning requirement. The course is also offered as a General Chemistry course to students in STEM majors that do not require taking Chemistry 200 (e.g. Food and Nutrition major). This course is also recommended as a preparatory course for students with limited mathematics and/or science background who plan to take higher level chemistry courses such as Chemistry 100, or students who plan to take the Chemistry Placement Exam for placement in Chemistry 200. Not open to students with credit in Chemistry 100 or 200.

Classics includes courses in Greek and Latin as well as non-language courses. Greek course numbers have a G suffix; Latin courses have an L suffix. No credit will be given for CLASS 101L, 202L, CLASS 303L, CLASS 304L taken out of sequence. Not open to students with credit in Classics 250L.
prerequisite_text: CLASS 101L.
enrollment_requirements: CLASS 101L.

subject: CLASS
title: Reading Latin Poetry
description: Reading classical poets such as Catullus or Ovid in original Latin. Attention to vocabulary, syntax, style, and historical-cultural context.
prerequisite_text: CLASS 303L. Junior or Senior standing.
enrollment_requirements: CLASS 303L. Junior or Senior standing.

subject: CLASS
title: Grk & Roman Myth & Legend
description: Great stories from the past. Heroes and heroines. Gods and goddesses. War and peace. Love and death. Adventure, romance, and peril in ancient literature, arts, and religion. Relevance and influence today.
prerequisite_text: Prerequisite(s) recommended: RWS 200. Junior or Senior standing.
enrollment_requirements: Prerequisite(s) recommended: RWS 200. Junior or Senior standing.

subject: CLASS
title: Epic & the Novel
description: Four classic works in the genre of epic and the novel in English translation; Homer's Iliad and Odyssey, Vergil's Aeneid, and Apuleius' Golden Ass. Literary criticism in historical-cultural contexts and relevance today.
prerequisite_text: Prerequisite(s) recommended: RWS 200. Junior or Senior standing.
enrollment_requirements: Prerequisite(s) recommended: RWS 200. Junior or Senior standing.

subject: CLASS
title: Gods, Gladiators, and Empire
description: Literary, artistic, and intellectual achievements of the ancient mediterranean world and beyond. Temples, tragedies, and texts. Priests, poets, and proconsuls. Great cultural traditions and influences.
prerequisite_text: Prerequisite(s) recommended: RWS 200. Junior or Senior standing.
enrollment_requirements: Prerequisite(s) recommended: RWS 200. Junior or Senior standing.

subject: CLASS
title: Sex Gender Erotic Ancient
description: Sexual lives of Greeks and Romans in classical art, literature, and material culture. Constructions of body aesthetics, desiring subjects and desired objects, the erotic, and gender norms. Modern receptions and theoretical interpretations of ancient sex.
prerequisite_text: Prerequisite(s) recommended: RWS 200. Junior or Senior standing.
enrollment_requirements: Prerequisite(s) recommended: RWS 200. Junior or Senior standing.

subject: E E
title: EMSofDigitizedPWRS
description: In recent decades, a growing number of digital solutions have been integrated to power transmission and distribution systems. These solutions include synchrophasors, inverter-based resources (IBRs), e.g., wind and solar, and grid edge intelligence, e.g., smart meters and smart thermostats. These digital solutions pose unprecedented challenges in grid management. Addressing these challenges requires power engineers to have a comprehensive yet in-depth understanding of the key functions of energy management systems (EMSs) of modern power systems. This course introduces the key functions of contemporary EMSs and promising technologies that have not been widely deployed in the contemporary EMSs. These functions include power system state estimations, and advanced techniques for grid monitoring and control. In addition, some trending topics cybersecurity, and artificial intelligence (AI) for power are also included in this course.

subject: ECON
title: Comparative Econ Systems
description: Current economic systems from primarily laissez-faire to state-controlled market economies with a focus on nations of Asia, Europe and Latin America; Soviet-style economic planning and transition to a market economy.
prerequisite_text: Six units of economics to include ECON 102. Junior or Senior standing.
enrollment_requirements: Six units of economics to include ECON 102. Junior or Senior standing.

subject: ECON
title: International Econ Prob
description: International problems, economic communities, organizations, and other selected topics.
prerequisite_text: ECON 101 and ECON 102.
enrollment_requirements: ECON 101 and ECON 102.

subject: ECON
title: Labor Economics
description: Labor force and mobility, human capital, labor demand, discrimination, determination of compensation and employment, productivity, impact of labor organizations, labor disputes, and social legislation.
prerequisite_text: ECON 321.
enrollment_requirements: ECON 321.

subject: ECON
title: Economics of Immigration
description: Examination and history of immigration policy in the United States and its intended and unintended consequences. Debates over economic assimilation, immigration policy, impact of native labor market, and perceptions about immigrants and the welfare system.
prerequisite_text: ECON 101 and ECON 321.
enrollment_requirements: ECON 101 and ECON 321.

subject: ECON
title: Econ Work Marriage Family
description: Economic analysis of marriage and labor supply; family-related changes in work behavior; gender differences in occupations and earnings; welfare, work and family policies in the U.S. and internationally; macroeconomic analysis of household structure and economy.
prerequisite_text: ECON 102.
enrollment_requirements: ECON 102.

subject: ECON
title: Public Finance
description: Principles and practices of taxation and public expenditures. Economic effects of public spending, debts and taxation. Financing social security and other services. Fiscal policy and prosperity. Relation to inflation and deflation. Special emphasis on social problems involved.
prerequisite_text: ECON 101 and ECON 102.
enrollment_requirements: ECON 101 and ECON 102.

subject: ECON
title: Health Economics
description: Apply economic principles and statistical techniques to production of health and delivery of health services. Business structures of delivery systems and incentives for providers and patients. Compare international health insurance systems, examine U.S. reforms.
prerequisite_text: ECON 101 and ECON 102; ECON 201 or STAT 119 or STAT 250; MATH 120, MATH 124, or MATH 150.
enrollment_requirements: ECON 101 and ECON 102; ECON 201 or STAT 119 or STAT 250; MATH 120, MATH 124, or MATH 150.

subject: ECON
title: Economics of Sports
description: Economic issues in professional and college team sports. Emphasis on monopoly and monopsony behavior by sports leagues and teams, public subsidies for sports facilities, ticket pricing, and NCAA rules and regulations.
prerequisite_text: ECON 102.
enrollment_requirements: ECON 102.

subject: ECON
title: Business Cycles
description: Fundamental factors in economic fluctuations. Examination of business cycle theories, and various policy proposals for economic stabilization. A consideration of current economic conditions and an examination of methods employed in preparing national economic forecasts.
prerequisite_text: ECON 101 and ECON 102.
enrollment_requirements: ECON 101 and ECON 102.

subject: ECON
title: Intro to Econometrics
description: Econometric techniques with emphasis on single-equation models. Applied skills learned through computer assignments.
prerequisite_text: ECON 301; MATH 120 or MATH 124 or MATH 150; Recommended: ECON 320 or ECON 321.
enrollment_requirements: ECON 301; MATH 120 or MATH 124 or MATH 150; Recommended: ECON 320 or ECON 321.

subject: ECON
title: Environmental Economics
description: Relation of environmental amenities and pollution to economic behavior and institutions. Environmental problems in externalities, public goods, and common-property resources. Environmental policy from perspective of public economics: regulation, benefit-cost analysis, valuation of non-market goods.
prerequisite_text: ECON 102.
enrollment_requirements: ECON 102.

subject: ECON
title: Econ of Natural Resources
description: Examination of efficient extraction and use of natural resources from an economic perspective. Fundamental and practical difference between renewable and non-renewable resources. Fossil fuel extraction, mining, renewable energy, forestry, fisheries, and conservation policy.
prerequisite_text: ECON 102.
enrollment_requirements: ECON 102.

subject: ECON
title: Econ of Financial Crises
description: Economic theories of crises and economic histories in qualitative and quantitative perspective to include recent crises in US and Europe. Empirical analysis of variety, frequency, and consequences. Policies for ending crises.
prerequisite_text: ECON 101 and ECON 102.
enrollment_requirements: ECON 101 and ECON 102.

subject: ECON
title: Econ Prblms of Mid East
description: Theories and practices of economic deveopment in the Middle East to include economic history, colonial legacies, natural resource curse, migration, state capitalism, and economics of conflict.
prerequisite_text: ECON 101 and ECON 102.
enrollment_requirements: ECON 101 and ECON 102.

subject: ECON
title: Law & Economics
description: Impact of legal rules on implicit prices for consumer and firm behavior, distribution of resources, economic efficiency. Background on laws surrounding property, contracts, torts, the judicial process, and crime, with focus on effects of laws on consumers and producers.
prerequisite_text: ECON 102.
enrollment_requirements: ECON 102.

subject: ECON
title: Econ of Strategy
description: Game theory and analysis of strategic decision making. Non-cooperative games in the context of business, bargaining among agents, political decision making, voting, etc.
prerequisite_text: ECON 321 and MATH 120 or MATH 124 or MATH 150.
enrollment_requirements: ECON 321 and MATH 120 or MATH 124 or MATH 150.

subject: ECON
title: Money and Banking
description: Money's measurement and use; monetary theory and policy; returns on financial instruments; international payments and foreign exchange; evolution of banking institutions, and global competition.
prerequisite_text: ECON 101, ECON 102, and ACCTG 201.
enrollment_requirements: ECON 101, ECON 102, and ACCTG 201.

subject: ECON
title: Economics Internship
description: Internship with business firms, nonprofit organizations and government agencies. Work done under joint direction of activity supervisor and instructor. Project report and internship conferences required. Maximum credit six units.
prerequisite_text: Consent of instructor.
enrollment_requirements: Consent of instructor.

subject: ECON
title: Regulation and Antitrust
description: This is a course on economic regulation and antitrust policy. In this course, we are primarily interested in the role of the government when economic efficiency fails. We will examine market structure and industrial organization.
prerequisite_text: ECON 101 and ECON 102
enrollment_requirements: ECON 101 and ECON 102

subject: ECON
title: Econ of Climate Change
description: This course applies economic tools to examine the causes and impacts of climate change, exploring how market and policy failures drive emissions and assessing the effectiveness and trade-offs of policies to mitigate global environmental and economic risks.
prerequisite_text: ECON 102
enrollment_requirements: ECON 102

subject: ECON
title: Special Study
description: Individual study. May be repeated for a maximum of six units. Maximum credit six units.
prerequisite_text: Consent of instructor.
enrollment_requirements: Consent of instructor.

subject: ECON
title: Mathematical Economics
description: Mathematical concepts as tools in understanding, developing, and illustrating economic theories. Applications of calculus and linear equations to constrained optimization, macro models, elasticity, general equilibrium, and input-output analysis.
prerequisite_text: MATH 124 or MATH 150. Recommended: ECON 320 or ECON 321.
enrollment_requirements: MATH 124 or MATH 150. Recommended: ECON 320 or ECON 321.

subject: ECON
title: Internation Mon Thry&Pol
description: International monetary spillovers from domestic macroeconomic policies. Foreign exchange markets and balance of payments. Fixed, flexible and managed exchange rates. Bretton Woods, international monetary fund, and world debt crisis.
prerequisite_text: ECON 320 or ECON 490.
enrollment_requirements: ECON 320 or ECON 490.

subject: ECON
title: Sem Appl Microecon Method
description: Decision-making techniques in applied microeconomics including cost-benefit analysis, choice under uncertainty and applied game theory techniques.
prerequisite_text: ECON 630.
enrollment_requirements: ECON 630.

subject: ECON
title: Appl Res in Econometrics
description: Econometric applications and techniques including discrete choice, panel data simultaneous equations and time series. Data analysis and statistical software training in STATA, SAS, and SPSS.
prerequisite_text: ECON 640.
enrollment_requirements: ECON 640.

subject: ECON
title: Internship in Econ
description: Students will be assigned to various jobs in which economic theory can be applied to decision making. Supervision will be shared by the graduate adviser and on-the-job supervisor.
prerequisite_text: ECON 630, ECON 640, and approval of graduate adviser.
enrollment_requirements: ECON 630, ECON 640, and approval of graduate adviser.

enrollment_requirements: ECON 630, ECON 640, and approval of graduate adviser.

description: Evil and how the language of evil has been used by diverse religious communities. Conceptions and portrayals of demons, hell, Satan, and vampires. Literature on the Holocaust, terrorism, torture, and war.
prerequisite_text: Junior or senior standing.
enrollment_requirements: Junior or senior standing.

prerequisite_text: Junior or senior standing.
enrollment_requirements: Junior or senior standing.

subject: HUM
title: Theory in the Humanities
description: Humanistic inquiry. Theories and theoretical debates across geographical borders. Foundational theories and recent interventions.
prerequisite_text: HUM 101, HUM 102, or upper division standing. Junior or Senior standing.
enrollment_requirements: HUM 101, HUM 102, or upper division standing. Junior or Senior standing.

subject: HUM
title: Health Justice Humanities
description: Fairness in healthcare; ethics and human rights in medical research/practice. Historical record of and artistic responses to medical abuses; racism, misogyny, and ableism in biomedicine.
prerequisite_text: Junior or senior standing.
enrollment_requirements: Junior or senior standing.

subject: I B
title: Internatl Bus Internship
description: Internships with international business firms, nonprofit organizations, and government agencies in U.S. and abroad. Work done under joint direction of activity sponsor and instructor. Project report and internship orientation required. Maximum credit six units with consent of instructor.
prerequisite_text: Consent of instructor; upper division standing in the major.
enrollment_requirements: Consent of instructor; upper division standing in the major.

subject: I B
title: Doing Business Internatn
description: Required business customs and protocol course pertinent to all regions.
prerequisite_text: Upper division status in the major.
enrollment_requirements: Upper division status in the major.

subject: I B
title: Doing Business Internatn
description: Required business customs and protocol course pertinent to all regions.
prerequisite_text: Upper division status in the major.
enrollment_requirements: Upper division status in the major.

subject: INT S
title: Seminar: Research Ethics
description: Core content areas that influence responsible conduct of research (RCR) including research misconduct, data management, use of animal and human subjects, conflict of interest and commitment, authorship, publication and peer review, and collaboration and mentoring. Intended for graduate students involved in research projects. Meets NIH and NSF training grant requirements for RCR instruction.
prerequisite_text: Graduate standing.
enrollment_requirements: Graduate standing.

subject: INT S
title: Special Study
description: Independent study. Maximum credit six units applicable to a master's degree.
prerequisite_text: Completion of Special Study Request Form.
enrollment_requirements: Completion of Special Study Request Form.

subject: INT S
title: Thesis
description: Preparation of a project or thesis for the master's degree.
prerequisite_text: An officially appointed thesis committee and advancement to candidacy.
enrollment_requirements: An officially appointed thesis committee and advancement to candidacy.

subject: INT S
title: Thesis Extension
description: Registration in any semester or term following assignment of RP in Course 799A in which the student expects to use the facilities and resources of the university; also the student must be registered in the course when the completed thesis or project is granted final approval.
prerequisite_text: Prior registration in Thesis 799A with an assigned grade symbol of RP.
enrollment_requirements: Prior registration in Thesis 799A with an assigned grade symbol of RP.

subject: INT S
title: Comprehensive Examination
description: Registration required of students whose only requirement is completion of the comprehensive examination for the master?s degree. Registration in 799C limited to two semesters.
prerequisite_text: Completion or concurrent enrollment in degree program courses.
enrollment_requirements: Completion or concurrent enrollment in degree program courses.

subject: ISCOR
title: Global Systems
description: Historical and contemporary examination of the global political, social, and economic order; examination of interaction of global forces with local and regional developments; studies of distinct contemporary and past global issues.
prerequisite_text: Junior or senior standing.
enrollment_requirements: Junior or senior standing.

subject: ISCOR
title: Conflict & Confl Resolutn
description: Examination of global, regional, and local dynamics that engender conflict, review of distinct diplomatic approaches (formal or informal) to resolve conflicts, case studies of past and ongoing conflicts.
prerequisite_text: Junior or senior standing.
enrollment_requirements: Junior or senior standing.

subject: ISCOR
title: Global Future: Climate
description: Examines impact of environmental changes on the global order; how environmental dynamics interact with political, economic, and social forces at the global, regional, and local levels; particular focus on the climate crisis.
prerequisite_text: Junior or senior standing.
enrollment_requirements: Junior or senior standing.

subject: ISCOR
title: Global Resistance
description: Study of global resistance movements in such areas as antimilitarism, economic justice, and social equality; includes a section on climate justice; attention to revolutionary and reformist theories of change at the global, regional, and local levels.
prerequisite_text: Junior or senior standing.
enrollment_requirements: Junior or senior standing.

subject: ISCOR
title: Alt Dispute Resolution
description: Theory of collaborative negotiation and mediation, practice of negotiation and mediation skills and techniques, and focus on personal styles of mediation and collaborative negotiating. Emphasis on resolving conflicts on the international level.
prerequisite_text: Upper division standing.
enrollment_requirements: Upper division standing.

subject: ISCOR
title: Internship in Iscor
description: Supervised internship of 150 hours in government or nongovernmental agency, office or business in an area directly related to international security and conflict resolution.
prerequisite_text: Senior standing. Nine units of international security and conflict resolution core courses and nine units in selected specialization. Consent of instructor.
enrollment_requirements: Senior standing. Nine units of international security and conflict resolution core courses and nine units in selected specialization. Consent of instructor.

subject: ISCOR
title: Thesis in Iscor
description: An original and comprehensive written description and analysis of a problem or problem area in international security and conflict resolution.
prerequisite_text: Senior standing. Nine units of international security and conflict resolution core courses and nine units in selected specialization. Consent of instructor.
enrollment_requirements: Senior standing. Nine units of international security and conflict resolution core courses and nine units in selected specialization. Consent of instructor.

subject: ISCOR
title: Special Study
description: Individual study. Maximum credit six units.
prerequisite_text: Consent of instructor. Six units of international security and conflict resolution core courses and six units in specialization.
enrollment_requirements: Consent of instructor. Six units of international security and conflict resolution core courses and six units in specialization.

subject: ITAL
title: Elementary Italian I
description: Pronunciation, speaking and writing, readings on Italian culture and civilization, essentials of grammar. subject: ITAL
title: Italian Food Culture
description: Interdisciplinary approaches to the study of food and foodways in Italian and Italian American culture, to include discussion of food practices, socialization, production, consumption, justice and sustainability.

subject: ITAL
title: Reading & Speaking Ital
description: Italian minors and international business majors are encouraged to enroll concurrently in ITAL 212 when available. Course uses language acquisition skills to help students understand cultural differences and develop a global perspective. Recommended for students wanting to satisfy the language graduation requirement. Emphasis on spoken language with readings of cultural material serving as a basis for discussion. Taught in Italian. Native speakers of Italian will not receive credit for taking lower division courses in Italian except with advance approval from the department. No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division Italian course taught in Italian. Italian 201 may only be taken after completing ITAL 100B, but may be taken concurrently with ITAL 211 or ITAL 212.
prerequisite_text: ITAL 100B or three years of high school Italian.
enrollment_requirements: ITAL 100B or three years of high school Italian.

subject: ITAL
title: Intermediate Italian II
description: Continuation of ITAL 211. Comprehensive review of Italian grammar and practice of all language skills at intermediate level within context of Italian culture. Course uses language acquisition skills to help students understand cultural differences and develop a global perspective. Italian minors and international business majors are encouraged to concurrently register in ITAL 201. Taught in Italian. Native speakers of Italian will not receive credit for taking lower division courses in Italian except with advance approval from the department. No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division Italian course taught in Italian. No credit will be given when ITAL 100A, ITAL 100B, ITAL 211, 212, and ITAL 301 are taken concurrently or out of sequence.
prerequisite_text: ITAL 211.
enrollment_requirements: ITAL 211.

subject: ITAL
title: Business Italian
description: Italian advertising, business culture, commercial practices and language, communication, cultural management, curation, current events, marketing entrepreneurship, social and digital media.
prerequisite_text: ITAL 212.
enrollment_requirements: ITAL 212.

subject: ITAL
title: Italian American Culture
description: Italian American experience of migration, identity formation, ethnic conflict, integration and assimilation, in a variety of genres and media, from literature to film, music and theatre, fiction and non-fiction. Taught in English.
prerequisite_text: Junior or Senior standing.
enrollment_requirements: Junior or Senior standing.

subject: ITAL
title: Internship
description: Practical work experience in a field related to Italian studies. Work done under joint direction of activity sponsor and instructor. Approved international internships may count toward international experience requirement for certain majors.
prerequisite_text: Upper division standing and consent of instructor.
enrollment_requirements: Upper division standing and consent of instructor.

subject: ITAL
title: Special Study
description: Individual study. Maximum credit six units. This course is intended only for students who are currently enrolled in or who already have credit for all upper division courses in Italian available in any given semester.
prerequisite_text: ITAL 301 and ITAL 305A or ITAL 305B.
enrollment_requirements: ITAL 301 and ITAL 305A or ITAL 305B.

title: Special Study

title: Third Year Japanese II
description: Further strengthening of communication skills in Japanese; various literary styles; introduction of chugaku kanji. Social and economic issues in Japan and the U.S.; cultural values shaping business conduct in Japan; characteristics of Japanese management; intercultural communication. Course uses language acquisition skills to help students understand cultural differences and develop a global perspective. Preparation for JAPAN 411. Taught in Japanese. No credit will be given for JAPAN 311, 312, JAPAN 411, JAPAN 412 taken out of sequence. No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division Japanese course taught in Japanese. prerequisite_text: JAPAN 311 or JAPAN 321. Junior or Senior standing.
enrollment_requirements: JAPAN 311 or JAPAN 321. Junior or Senior standing.

subject: JAPAN
title: Adv Conversatn Thr Media

prerequisite_text: JAPAN 311 or JAPAN 321. Junior or Senior standing.
enrollment_requirements: JAPAN 311 or JAPAN 321. Junior or Senior standing.

subject: JAPAN
title: Fourth Year Japanese II
description: Continuation of Japanese 411. Further strengthening of communication skills in Japanese; various literary styles; most joyo kanji. prerequisite_text: JAPAN 411 or JAPAN 421.
enrollment_requirements: JAPAN 411 or JAPAN 421.

subject: JAPAN
title: Newspaper Read & Adv Comp
description: Development of reading and writing skills through texts taken from current Japanese newspapers and broadcast news.
prerequisite_text: JAPAN 411 or JAPAN 421.
enrollment_requirements: JAPAN 411 or JAPAN 421.

title: Writing for Mass Media
description: Introduction to writing techniques for mass media. Laboratory practice in informational and persuasive writing, evaluation, and judgment. In some semesters, specially designated sections require bilingual fluency in English and Spanish, to be determined by a stamp of Spanish/English biliteracy on high school transcript, or a score of 5 on AP Spanish test, or passing the SDSU Spanish Language Proficiency Test. subject: NURS
title: PMH-NP: Mental Health Theory I
description: Focuses on theoretical content and clinical practice guidelines for assessment and treatment of psychiatric disorders across the lifespan. Emphasis on therapeutic communication principles, techniques, and ethics, as well as health promotion and disease, promoting recovery and resilience, and reducing stigma.
prerequisite_text: NURS 806, NURS 807, NURS 808.
enrollment_requirements: NURS 806, NURS 807, NURS 808.

subject: NURS
title: PMH-NP: Mental Hlth Pract I-A
description: Supervised clinical experiences allowing synthesis of advanced clinical competencies in the PMHNP role, including psychiatric assessment, diagnosing, case conceptualization across the lifespan. Develop communication skills, including motivation interviewing techniques and apply advanced theoretical knowledge within an interprofessional team.
prerequisite_text: NURS 806, NURS 807, NURS 808; Concurrent with NURS 809.
enrollment_requirements: NURS 806, NURS 807, NURS 808; Concurrent with NURS 809.

title: Epi, Population & Global Hlth

Construction of why epidemiology is the cornerstone of public health through application of descriptive, analytic, and experimental analysis.
prerequisite_text: Admission to DNP program and consent of School of Nursing Graduate Advisor.
enrollment_requirements: Admission to DNP program and consent of School of Nursing Graduate Advisor.

title: Statistical Meth in Psych
description: Quantitative methods in psychology for producing, analyzing, and interpreting data. description: Natural science exploration of surf-related topics to include high-quality surfing waves in the ocean and in human-made surf lagoons, surfboard evolution from hand-carved lumber to recycled ocean plastics, and climate change resilience and surf ecosystem conservation.

title: Travel and Self-awareness
description: How recreation and travel are influenced by economic, environmental, political, and socio-cultural forces. Impacts of recreation and travel on well-being and self-awareness.

enrollment_requirements: Consent of instructor or department chair and 125 hours experience in recreation leadership.

subject: RUSSN
title: Beginning Russian 2
description: Continuation of RUSSN 100A. Course uses language acquisition skills to help students understand cultural differences and develop a global perspective. Taught in Russian. Native speakers of Russian will not receive credit for taking lower division courses in Russian except with advance approval from the department. No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division Russian course taught in Russian. No credit will be given for RUSSN 100A, RUSSN 100B, RUSSN 200A, RUSSN 200B, RUSSN 301 taken out of sequence.
prerequisite_text: RUSSN 100A or two years of high school Russian.
enrollment_requirements: RUSSN 100A or two years of high school Russian.

subject: RUSSN
title: Intermediate Russian 2
description: Continuation of RUSSN 200A. Course uses language acquisition skills to help students understand cultural differences and develop a global perspective. Taught in Russian. prerequisite_text: RUSSN 200A.
enrollment_requirements: RUSSN 200A.

subject: RUSSN
title: Russian Culture and Society
description: Examines Russian culture and identity from Imperial times to today. Students analyze primary sources exploring autocracy, religion, gender, empire, nature, ecology, and memory while investigating how cultural practices shape and reflect evolving definitions of Russian national identity. Taught in English.
prerequisite_text: Junior or Senior standing
enrollment_requirements: Junior or Senior standing

enrollment_requirements: Upper division standing in major and consent of instructor.

prerequisite_text: RUSSN 301.
enrollment_requirements: RUSSN 301.

description: Further practice in writing, reading, and critical thinking. Emphasis on rhetoric of written arguments in context and using multiple sources in writing. Continued attention to structure, cohesion, and rhetorical conventions. Not open to students with credit in AFRAS 200, AMIND 225, CCS 200, ECL 200, or LING 200. International students are advised to take LING 200. Completion of RWS 200 may require completion of the library workbook assignment.
prerequisite_text: Satisfaction of the SDSU Written Communication Assessment requirement and completion of one of the following courses with a grade of C- or better: AAS 150 or AFRAS 120 or AMIND 120 or CCS 111B or LING 100B or RWS 100 [or ECL 100 or RWS 105B.

subject: RWS
title: Rhet in Everyday Life
description: Rhetorical analysis of written, visual, and electronic texts. How rhetorical theories and perspectives help us understand the workings of popular culture, political discourse, visual images, legal arguments, social media, and other texts encountered in everyday life.
prerequisite_text: Review the SDSU Catalog for prerequisite requirements. Proof of completing the prerequisites may be required on the first day of classes.
enrollment_requirements: Review the SDSU Catalog for prerequisite requirements. Proof of completing the prerequisites may be required on the first day of classes.

subject: RWS
title: Business Writing and Rhetoric
description: Effective writing and rhetoric in business and organizational settings, including letters, memos, and reports. Features organization, drafting, revision, and editing of documents and presentations.

subject: RWS
title: Writing in Various Settings
description: Composing effective texts for a wide range of situations in and out of the university. Learning to adjust textual elements for specific purposes, audiences, and settings. Enhances critical reading and writing skills by exploring how content contributes to meaning and effectiveness. Satisfies the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement (GWAR) for students who get a minimum grade of C or Cr. Upper-division courses should only be taken by students who have completed 60 semester units or more. In exceptional cases, a student who has completed fewer than 60 units may enroll in upper division courses. International students are advised to take LING 305W.

enrollment_requirements: SOC 201 and SOC 101 or SOC 102; or Social Science major.

subject: SOC
title: Cult Origins of Surf
description: Surfing from Hawaiian origins to the early 20th century. Special emphasis upon cultural differences between Polynesian and Western societies. Phenomenology of surfing.
prerequisite_text: Junior or senior standing.
enrollment_requirements: Junior or senior standing.

subject: SOC
title: Soc of Popular Culture
description: Forms and features of popular culture. Distinctions between highbrow and lowbrow cultures. Sociological theories about effects, functions, and power of popular culture in society and in social change.
prerequisite_text: Junior or senior standing.
enrollment_requirements: Junior or senior standing.

subject: SOC
title: Sociology of Religion
description: Forms of religious belief, knowledge, practice, and experience tied to different social arrangements and historical periods. Consequences of religion for community and society. Secularization and conversion processes in modern industrial societies.
prerequisite_text: SOC 101. Junior or Senior standing.
enrollment_requirements: SOC 101. Junior or Senior standing.

title: Sociology of Religion

subject: SOC
title: Global Social Problems
description: Contemporary social problems from global and transnational perspectives.
prerequisite_text: Junior or senior standing.
enrollment_requirements: Junior or senior standing.

subject: SOC
title: Soc of Race & Ethnicity
description: Historical and comparative analysis of race and ethnic relations. Origins and maintenance of ethnic stratification systems; discrimination and prejudice; the adaptation of communities; role of social movements and government policies in promoting civil rights and social change.
prerequisite_text: Junior or senior standing.
enrollment_requirements: Junior or senior standing.

subject: SOC
title: Classical Social Theory
description: Classical theories of society. Intellectual history of European and U.S. theoretical developments in functionalism, historical materialism, historicism, positivism, and symbolic interactionism. Theories of modernity and evolution of modern world system.
prerequisite_text: SOC 101.
enrollment_requirements: SOC 101.

subject: SOC
title: Contemp Social Theory
description: Contemporary theories of society. Intellectual history of U.S. and European theoretical developments in critical race theory, critical theory, feminist theory, post-structuralism, structural functionalism, and structuralism. Theories of postmodernity and non-Western theories of cultural and economic hegemony.
prerequisite_text: SOC 101.
enrollment_requirements: SOC 101.

subject: SOC
title: Surv&Exper Research Meth
description: Research process from research design through data processing, analysis, and interpretation. Quantitative research techniques including universe enumeration, sampling, questionnaire construction, scaling techniques, structured interviews, and experimental designs.
prerequisite_text: SOC 301.
enrollment_requirements: SOC 301.

subject: SOC
title: Qualitative Research Meth
description: Ethnographic research methods including interviewing, observation, participant observation, and case studies. Problems in research design; gaining and maintaining rapport; analysis, interpretation, and writing with qualitative data.
prerequisite_text: SOC 301.
enrollment_requirements: SOC 301.

subject: SOC
title: Soc Psy Mind Self&Society
description: Major theories, problems, and findings concerning the relationship of the individual and society. Topics include consciousness and construction of meaning, self-concept and social identity, socialization and interaction, group behavior and group membership.
prerequisite_text: Junior or senior standing.
enrollment_requirements: Junior or senior standing.

subject: SOC
title: Soc Psy Mind Self&Society
description: Major theories, problems, and findings concerning the relationship of the individual and society. Topics include consciousness and construction of meaning, self-concept and social identity, socialization and interaction, group behavior and group membership.
prerequisite_text: Junior or senior standing.
enrollment_requirements: Junior or senior standing.

subject: SOC
title: Soc Construction Reality
description: Analysis of reality as an ongoing social process. Creation and internalization of social worlds through language. Common sense and the multiple realities of everyday life. Dynamic emergence of social structure.
prerequisite_text: SOC 101.
enrollment_requirements: SOC 101.

subject: SOC
title: Latina/o Sociology
description: Sociological history of the Hispanic/Latino category, racial and national diversity of Latinx populations, critiques of the Latinx category, and social problems affecting Latinxs. Sociological studies examining immigration and racial classification systems in the U.S. and Latin America.
prerequisite_text: Junior or Senior standing
enrollment_requirements: Junior or Senior standing

subject: SOC
title: Sexuality Modern Society
description: Social construction of sexualities. Sexual behaviors, desires, and practices. Changing norms of sexuality, morality and social control, non-normative sexualities, sexual identities, and social and political movements regarding sexuality.
prerequisite_text: SOC 101.
enrollment_requirements: SOC 101.

subject: SOC
title: Gender & Sexuality in Korea
description: Issues related to gender and sexuality in Korean history; gender relations in family, workplace, popular culture, politics; non-normative genders and sexualities; how gender and sexuality intersect with race, nationality, ethnicity, and class; social and political movements regarding gender and sexuality. Same course as ASIAN 429 and KOR 429.
prerequisite_text: Junior or senior standing.
enrollment_requirements: Junior or senior standing.

subject: SOC
title: Social Organization
description: Social structure of societies. Historical examination of structure and development of social institutions, communities, and other large scale organizations.
prerequisite_text: Junior or senior standing.
enrollment_requirements: Junior or senior standing.

subject: SOC
title: Wealth, Status & Power
description: Social inequality as an institutional process. Patterns of unequal distribution of wealth, power, privilege and prestige, their causes, and impact this has on communities and societies.
prerequisite_text: SOC 101.
enrollment_requirements: SOC 101.

subject: SOC
title: Wealth, Status & Power
description: Social inequality as an institutional process. Patterns of unequal distribution of wealth, power, privilege and prestige, their causes, and impact this has on communities and societies.
prerequisite_text: SOC 101.
enrollment_requirements: SOC 101.

subject: SOC
title: Sociology Mental Illness
description: Social, cultural, historical, and political factors involved in definition of "madness" and theories of mental illness in various societies. Review of research about incidence, prevalence, and social epidemiology of mental illness, as a community problem, and its distribution by social class, gender, age, geographical region, and country.
prerequisite_text: SOC 101.
enrollment_requirements: SOC 101.

subject: SOC
title: Sociology Mental Illness
description: Social, cultural, historical, and political factors involved in definition of "madness" and theories of mental illness in various societies. Review of research about incidence, prevalence, and social epidemiology of mental illness, as a community problem, and its distribution by social class, gender, age, geographical region, and country.
prerequisite_text: SOC 101.
enrollment_requirements: SOC 101.

subject: SOC
title: Crime and Society
description: Social origins, forms, and functions of criminal law. Sociological theories about causes and consequences of crime. Measurement and distribution of violent crimes, property crimes, victimless crimes, white collar crime, and their impact on communities and society.
prerequisite_text: SOC 101.
enrollment_requirements: SOC 101.

subject: SOC
title: Crime and Society
description: Social origins, forms, and functions of criminal law. Sociological theories about causes and consequences of crime. Measurement and distribution of violent crimes, property crimes, victimless crimes, white collar crime, and their impact on communities and society.
prerequisite_text: SOC 101.
enrollment_requirements: SOC 101.

subject: SOC
title: Sociology of Deviance
description: Conformity and nonconformity; the relationship between individual liberty and social control; stigma and the labeling of deviant behavior such as prostitution, alcoholism, drug addiction, and crime.

subject: SOC
title: Soc of Criminal Orgs
description: Major criminal organizations that operate in underworld across time, space, and socio-cultural context, including Mafia, Yakuza, Triads, and transnational drug traffickers and human smugglers. Explore their social organizations, operations, roles, and identities.

subject: SOC
title: Urban Sociology
description: Cities and neighborhoods as they pertain to day-to-day life. Location?s importance for life outcomes and what social forces can shape location.
prerequisite_text: SOC 101.
enrollment_requirements: SOC 101.

subject: SOC
title: Social Change
description: Social change at the interpersonal, institutional, and societal levels of analysis. Major economic, political, technological, and demographic forces that have shaped the contemporary world. Topics may include modernization, industrialization, urbanization, revolution, and prospects of social change in rich and poor nations.
prerequisite_text: Junior or senior standing.
enrollment_requirements: Junior or senior standing.

subject: SOC
title: Soc of Intersectionality
description: Social inequality to include current research on class, gender, and race. Interlocking systems of privilege and oppression and their impact on society.
prerequisite_text: SOC 101.
enrollment_requirements: SOC 101.

subject: SOC
title: Protests,Reforms & Revol
description: Revolutionary and reform movements in relationship to the larger society. Conditions leading to development of social movements, emergence of leadership, ideologies, strategies, recruitment of members, and social consequences; case studies.
prerequisite_text: SOC 101.
enrollment_requirements: SOC 101.

subject: SOC
title: Protests,Reforms & Revol
description: Revolutionary and reform movements in relationship to the larger society. Conditions leading to development of social movements, emergence of leadership, ideologies, strategies, recruitment of members, and social consequences; case studies.
prerequisite_text: SOC 101.
enrollment_requirements: SOC 101.

subject: SOC
title: Technology and Society
description: Social construction of technological systems. Emergent technologies within particular cultural forms, social structures, and political practices, and how these phenomena influence design and use of technology. Technology as a mode of social experience.
prerequisite_text: Junior or senior standing.
enrollment_requirements: Junior or senior standing.

subject: SOC
title: Soc Research Comm Engage
description: Division of labor in sociology, theories of organizations and social change, labor market trends frame internship experience. Students will be required to complete 45 hours of outside supervised research or internship.
prerequisite_text: Junior level or senior level.
enrollment_requirements: Junior level or senior level.

title: Field Internship
description: Supervised field placement of students in community agencies. Practical experiences related to studies within the sociology curriculum. Maximum credit six units.
prerequisite_text: SOC 101.
enrollment_requirements: SOC 101.

subject: SOC
title: Special Study
description: Individual study. Maximum credit six units.
prerequisite_text: Consent of instructor.
enrollment_requirements: Consent of instructor.

subject: SOC
title: Immigrants and Refugees
description: Contemporary migration to the United States, especially from Latin America and Asia. Political and economic migration. Immigrant and refugee adaptation. Theoretical controversies, research applications, and policy implications.
prerequisite_text: SOC 101.
enrollment_requirements: SOC 101.

subject: SOC
title: Investigation and Report
description: Analysis of special topics in sociology. Maximum credit six units.
prerequisite_text: Fifteen units in sociology and consent of instructor.
enrollment_requirements: Fifteen units in sociology and consent of instructor.

title: Adv Cntmp Soc Thry: Core
description: Examination and analysis of original works in modern/postmodern sociological theory.
prerequisite_text: Graduate standing.
enrollment_requirements: Graduate standing.

title: Adv Qualt Methods: Core
description: Qualitative methods for data collection, analysis, and reporting in contemporary sociological research and related disciplines. Study, practice, critiques of techniques; ethnography, interviews, archival research, content analysis.
prerequisite_text: Graduate standing and credit or concurrent registration in SOC 600.
enrollment_requirements: Graduate standing and credit or concurrent registration in SOC 600.

subject: SOC
title: Top Directed Read
description: Selected reading providing coverage of social theory, social disorganization, social organization, social institutions, social psychology (sociological approaches), community research methods, population and demography, or special topics. Maximum credit three units applicable to a master's degree.
prerequisite_text: Credit or concurrent registration in at least one core course or one seminar.
enrollment_requirements: Credit or concurrent registration in at least one core course or one seminar.

subject: RWS
title: Writing in Various Settings
description: Composing effective texts for a wide range of situations in and out of the university. Learning to adjust textual elements for specific purposes, audiences, and settings. Enhances critical reading and writing skills by exploring how content contributes to meaning and effectiveness. Satisfies the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement (GWAR) for students who get a minimum grade of C or Cr. Upper-division courses should only be taken by students who have completed 60 semester units or more. In exceptional cases, a student who has completed fewer than 60 units may enroll in upper division courses. International students are advised to take LING 305W.

subject: SOC

description: This course is prerequisite to all upper division courses in sociology. Major ideas, concepts, and methods in the study of society to include socialization, culture, social structure, social stratification, deviance, social control, and social change.
prerequisite_text: Review the SDSU Catalog for prerequisite requirements. Proof of completing the prerequisites may be required on the first day of classes.
enrollment_requirements: Review the SDSU Catalog for prerequisite requirements. Proof of completing the prerequisites may be required on the first day of classes.

subject: SOC
title: Intro to Social Problems
description: Contemporary social problems. Topics may include poverty, inequality, unemployment, crime and deviance, population and ecological problems, health, family issues, and the role of ideology and interest groups in the definition of social problems.
prerequisite_text: Review the SDSU Catalog for prerequisite requirements. Proof of completing the prerequisites may be required on the first day of classes.
enrollment_requirements: Review the SDSU Catalog for prerequisite requirements. Proof of completing the prerequisites may be required on the first day of classes.

prerequisite_text: SOC 201 and SOC 101 or SOC 102; or Social Science major.
enrollment_requirements: SOC 201 and SOC 101 or SOC 102; or Social Science major.

subject: SOC
title: Cult Origins of Surf
description: Surfing from Hawaiian origins to the early 20th century. Special emphasis upon cultural differences between Polynesian and Western societies. Phenomenology of surfing.
prerequisite_text: Junior or senior standing.
enrollment_requirements: Junior or senior standing.

subject: SOC
title: Soc of Race & Ethnicity
description: Historical and comparative analysis of race and ethnic relations. Origins and maintenance of ethnic stratification systems; discrimination and prejudice; the adaptation of communities; role of social movements and government policies in promoting civil rights and social change.
prerequisite_text: Junior or senior standing.
enrollment_requirements: Junior or senior standing.

subject: SOC
title: Wealth, Status & Power
description: Social inequality as an institutional process. Patterns of unequal distribution of wealth, power, privilege and prestige, their causes, and impact this has on communities and societies.
prerequisite_text: SOC 101.
enrollment_requirements: SOC 101.

subject: SOC
title: Homicide in America
description: Characteristics and distribution of murder, including historical and cross-cultural comparisons. Social psychological, structural, cultural and situational explanations of causes and consequences of juvenile, gang, domestic, mass, serial and sexual murders.

subject: SOC
title: American Labor Movement
description: Social history of the American labor movement from late eighteenth century to present. Relationship between the labor movement, the labor process, and the state. Race and gender divisions within the labor movement.
prerequisite_text: SOC 101.
enrollment_requirements: SOC 101.
